caption: Kar. 129. Stela
labels: 6 sic, by line 6 (over the se at the start of line 6)
reading: (1)wosi : soreyi : kdi : (2)qebtse lowi : boẖeye (3)ted?ḫlowi : dkret(4)ri : mẖewitr : te(5)rikelowi : pe : (6)setol : yetmde(7)lo
notes: Line 2 of the copy: te is followed by an outlined chip (not hatched); the next sign (rising stroke with hook, read d) runs into it, so no lost sign is marked. Line 3 of the copy: an outlined chip between terike and lowi, nothing marked lost. 'kdi': first sign is a flat-topped 3 with long tail (k, could be p). In 'tedḫlowi' the sign before o is small (l), so no e. 'd?om?eye': the first sign is a nu with a hook (d or b); the 3-shape could be s or ẖ. 'm?sewitr': first sign is the ℸ form of m. 'p?l': long-tailed Σ sign, p or k. Line 6 is marked sic by Griffith over ʋ// (se). Text ends at yetmdelo with no divider.
check_notes: All 17 entries placed. Griffith's (s) in pese(s)tol is a restoration not in the copy. tedḫlowi (no e) and the outlined chips are not covered by any entry.

caption: Kar. 130. Altar
labels: sic, by line 12 (over the ḫ of pḫrẖte)
reading: wosi : (2)soreyi : (3)[.]men?t?yd?lowi : (4)pedemedoke : te(5)dḫlowi : ḫ?rpḫñ : (6)tedoke : (7)terike(8)lowi : pe(9)setoli : (10)kditowi : (11)atomẖe : psiẖte : (12)atmẖe : pḫrkte
notes: The divider after soreyi is partly hatched; line number 3 stands over it. Line 3 of the stone: hatching before and after a hatched 3-shape (read s?) and a hatched 4-like sign (i?); n has a long tail; t? is a small 3 with a dot. The R-shaped sign (rising stroke + loop) is read d throughout (it is the d of tedḫelowi in Kar. 132 and Sh. 3); in pedemtdoke and tedoke it could be n. 'w?rkḫd': first sign is a closed loop with tail, w or to. Line 9/10 words: the L-shaped sign is read ḫ (could be d in its ℓ form); a dot stands after the L in kd?iḫ?wi. Line 11: L-shaped sign read to (ato mẖe formula); the final te is hatched on its slash. Line 12: Griffith marks the ḫ sic and a dot stands between p and ḫ.
check_notes: All entries placed. Leading [.] kept: the copy hatches before m though the type starts with m. Index A prints 'pesetol k ditowi' with a space; Index B pese(s)toli kditowi.

caption: Kar. 131. Stela with male figure (Kar. Cem., Pl. 12, No. 7086)
notes: Two lines without dividers or line numbers. The lower line begins with wosi soreyi, so it is read first; the upper line is read second. Lower line ends with two nu-like signs around a slash: the right one has a hooked arm (b?), the left one plain (d?). Upper line: '//3' groups are read q + o (the q sign /3 followed by o), as in -qowi; the second group is a bold 3 (m? or ẖ) with a thin small S beside it (e?), drawn lighter. A large N-shaped sign stands under the right end of the lower line, apart from the text; not included in the reading (it may be a sign n or a mark).
check_notes: All entries placed. Reading order reversed from step 1: Index C gives wosi and soreyi as line 2 (131/2).

caption: Sh. 1. Altar (Areika, Pl. 32, No. 5100)
reading: wosiasoreyi tlye(2)qowi [.] kidteliye tedḫ?[.](3)lowi tẖeye (4)terikelowi : (5)snmdese teñ(6)tel yetmde(7)lowi : mlomrse (8)teñtelowi a(9)tomẖe psoẖe atmḫe : psi(11)ḫrto ḫmlol : (12)psitḫto ḫl(13)ẖl psiẖolto
notes: Most word ends have no divider in this copy; spaces mark clear gaps. After wosi stands an S with a long-tailed 2 (read a; could be k+e). t?i?: a 5-shape with a dot, then a hatched 4. The sign after the first te in line 2 group is read d (R-shape); ḫ? in line 3 is a U-shaped sign followed by hatching (one lost sign, probably e). The '·5' at the start of line 4 group read t? with s? (closed 3). Line 5 starts with a barred 3 (k?) and an inverted-V with long tail (n). The crossed sign in ted?te (lines 6, 8) is read d (it could be ñ). mlomrse?: the last sign is partly hatched (se?). Line numbers 10 not found on the copy. Lines 11-13: shapes of 3, 5 and the small hook are uncertain (s/m/ẖ, e/l); the formula words are read sign by sign.

caption: Sh. 2. Altar (Areika, Pl. 32, No. 5101)
reading: wosi?a(2)s[.]reyi : (3)ḫwitn?[.][.][.]qowi : tẖ(4)rot?ikde : tedḫelowi (5)qeremye te?[.][.][.]i? k?[.](6)[.][.]w?i : a(sic)mẖe[.] (7)p[.]soẖ : a(8)tmẖe[.] p[.]ḫr?[.] [.]mlo(9)l ẖol[.]
notes: Heavy hatching. Line 1: hatching on the i of wosi; the o of soreyi is hatched away. Line 3: first sign is c with a stroke (ḫ? or to); a long hatched stretch of about three signs before q. Line 4 group: the first two signs are hatched (t?, m?). A hatched mark stands at the left end of the tedḫelowi line where a divider would be; not counted. Line 5/6: two hatched stretches (about three signs each) with a hatched i? and a hatched k with long tail; line number 6 stands over the hatching. Line 7: Griffith marks sic over the e-part of 'a' (the text has a mẖe with no t). The formula 'p..s/s' recurs in Sh. 1 and Sh. 3 (/3 could be q). Line 8 group: after ḫ a nu with a hooked arm (b?), then hatching. Last line: about 1-2 hatched signs at the right end, one hatched sign at the left end.
check_notes: All entries but psiẖebḫte placed. Formula A 'a(sic)' as Griffith prints it.

Line 3 group: 'aḫ?e': S + long-tailed 2 (a), then an L-shaped sign (ḫ?). In tedḫeli? the word ends with a small hook and 4 (no o, w). In te(4)dḫe?e?lowi there are two S-shapes between ḫ and l.
